newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says U.S. police beat up its diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Russia says U.S. police beat up its diplomat.

text.p: Russia said on Tuesday that U.S. police had beaten and arrested one of its diplomats in New York and demanded an apology from Washington.

A Foreign Ministry statement said the first secretary of Russia's permanent representation at the United Nations was dragged from his car and beaten by police on December 29 despite showing his identification.

It said police broke the hand of the diplomat, named as Boris Obnosov, smashed his glasses and tore his clothes before handcuffing him and taking him to a police station where he was held for 30 minutes.
It gave no further details of the incident and no one at the U.S. embassy was immediately available for comment.
The U.S. Charge d'Affaires to Moscow was summoned to the ministry on Tuesday to hear the protest, the statement said.
"The Russian side views the incident with concern. The American diplomat was told that we insist on an official apology from the American side," it said.
